title: Client adaptation playbook for Unified Inference API consolidation
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Background: We are consolidating several legacy inference endpoints and client compatibility shims into a single Unified Inference API that simplifies routing, reduces maintenance surface area, and enables consistent observability and billing. This ticket is the PM playbook and acceptance criteria for the client-facing migration: what we will require of clients, what we will provide (shims, SDK patches, telemetry), and the timeline and risk controls for the deprecation window.

Scope:
- Affects legacy endpoints: /v0/completions, /v1/legacy-chat, older embed endpoints (internal mapping list maintained in links).
- Does NOT include model deprecations of first-party models scheduled separately (those will be referenced).
- Includes SDK changes, docs, migration tooling, and support runbooks.
- Includes telemetry changes to detect non-migrated clients and generate alerts.

Objectives:
1) Provide clear, low-effort migration paths for 80% of active clients within a 60 day notification window.
2) Offer an automated compatibility adapter for self-hosted SDKs and a one-line patch for server-side wrappers.
3) Ensure no production outages caused by the switch; all client failures must fall back to safe-mode routing for 48 hours after GA.

Non-goals:
- Major rewrites of partner integrations (we will offer engineering-assist for top 10 accounts but not rewrite partner code).
- Simultaneous model architecture changes unrelated to endpoint consolidation.
acceptance_criteria: Public migration guide published and linked in console by 2026-03-20
SDK patches published for JavaScript, Python, Go with semantic version bump and migration guides in each SDK repo
Compatibility adapter (server-side middleware) implemented and released as open-source under redwood-org/compat-adapters; demo integration in examples repo
Telemetry signals created: 'legacy_endpoint_usage', 'migration_attempt', and 'compat_adapter_active' with dashboard and alert when legacy usage > 5% of baseline
Canary rollout completed against 5% of traffic with no increase in 5xx errors or latency SLO violations for 72 hours
Support runbook and escalation paths created; Tier 1 and Solutions Engineering briefed and tabletop exercised
Migration metrics measured: 80% of active API keys migrated or using compat-adapter within 60-day notification window
Hard deprecation date announced at least 30 days before enforcement and enforced by routing change that returns 410 for non-migrated keys after grace period
migration_plan: Phase 0 (Docs & Tools) - 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-20: publish migration guide, include code diffs for common languages, mapping table of old->new endpoints and model equivalence recommendations
Phase 1 (SDK & Adapter) - 2026-03-15 to 2026-04-05: release SDK patches with feature flag defaulting to old behavior; publish open-source server-side compatibility adapter and Docker image
Phase 2 (Early Access) - 2026-04-06 to 2026-04-20: invite partners and high-usage customers to canary; collect feedback and iterate on adapter; special support offered to top 10 customers
Phase 3 (GA & Telemetry) - 2026-04-21 to 2026-05-01: enable opt-in GA routing to Unified API for all migrated keys; dashboards live; automated migration suggestions surfaced in Console

Phase 4 (Enforcement) - 2026-05-02 to 2026-05-31: 30-day enforcement window where non-migrated keys receive deprecation headers and warnings; 2026-06-01 hard cutover where non-migrated keys receive 410 with migration link
Rollback plan: a capacity-limited fallback route to legacy runtime retained for 48 hours post-GA; operator can toggle routing and extend grace period by 7 days if significant regressions are observed
rollout_timeline: 2026-03-10: Internal announcement and begin docs drafts
2026-04-06: Canary invitations sent to 50 orgs (mix of self-serve and enterprise)
2026-04-21: GA opt-in switch available in Console (customers can toggle)
2026-06-01: Hard deprecation enforcement; non-migrated clients receive 410 responses
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Large customers with customized wrappers can't migrate in time. Mitigation: Solutions Engineering ownership for top 10 accounts; white-glove migration plans and temporary routing exemptions.

Risk: Hidden SDK forks used by customers bypass official patch. Mitigation: Provide compatibility adapter and easy-to-integrate middleware; detect via telemetry and contact account owner with suggested patch.

Risk: Unforeseen latency regressions after routing change. Mitigation: Canary against 5% traffic with latency SLO gating and immediate rollback path; capacity-limited legacy route for 48 hours post-GA.
Risk: Increased support volume. Mitigation: Pre-populated support article templates, automated checklist in Support console, 72-hour staffing spike for L2/SE during GA and enforcement windows.
